[DEBATE INCOMPLETE - phases 1-5 of 11 ran; phases 7-11 blocked by an API spend limit. No Judge verdict exists. The notes below are VERIFIED FINDINGS from the debate record, not an adjudicated recommendation.]

VERIFIED (reproduced by the Defender, not merely argued):
- render_report.py:90-97 sums approx_tokens over {SCRIPT, HYBRID} and prints it as "removes ~N
  tokens of per-run reasoning", but SKILL.md Step 8 explicitly RETAINS HYBRID prose. On this
  fixture 119 of 202 claimed tokens (59 percent) is prose the skill promises to keep. Every run
  prints this line. Both sides converged on deleting the figure, not correcting it.
- The proposed scripts consume .work/topics.json and .work/stats.json and emit a `url` field,
  none of which any step in the fixture produces. No validator checks input provenance.

DEBATE MOVEMENT: Adversary dropped 1 of 5 objections and narrowed 2 after the Advocate found its
provenance check inspected `interface` only, while `url` lives in `stdout`. The Advocate then
conceded the repaired check and conceded exit-1, citing this run's own report.md L72 as proof the
soft version fails in practice.

DISCRIMINATION: with-skill 7/7, baseline 6/7. The one separating assertion rewards scriptify's own
output schema. The baseline independently classified all three tool-gated steps HYBRID.

[DEBATE INCOMPLETE - phases 1-5 of 11 ran; phases 7-11 blocked by an API spend limit. No Judge verdict exists. The notes below are VERIFIED FINDINGS from the debate record, not an adjudicated recommendation.]

VERIFIED:
- Neither fence counter is correct. CommonMark truth on a 4-case fixture is 2/1/1/0 (total 4);
  with-skill docs_stats.py gives 3/1/0/1 (total 5); baseline lint_docs.py gives 2/0/0/0 (total 2).
  "Count the fenced code blocks" is unspecified anywhere, and contract-first CANNOT catch an
  unspecified semantic, because one run authors both the fixture and the implementation. The 16/16
  green certifies self-consistency, not correctness.
- No collision detection exists in scriptify's tooling: inventory.py collects every existing script
  path, render_report.py reads only inv["steps"] and never joins them. "Collision" appears exactly
  once in the whole skill (SKILL.md L160).
- POSSIBLE EVAL INVALIDITY: this harness's Write refuses to overwrite an unread file, so the
  scenario may be unable to distinguish the skill's guard from the tool's.

CORRECTION TO THE RECORD: the two-script split predates the collision (report.md L52-54), so the
Judge's Q1 premise and the Defender's concession to it are both factually wrong.

[DEBATE INCOMPLETE - phases 1-5 of 11 ran; phases 7-11 blocked by an API spend limit. No Judge verdict exists. The notes below are VERIFIED FINDINGS from the debate record, not an adjudicated recommendation.]

VERIFIED - the most severe finding in the suite:
- Relocate the skill, replace all 7 scripts with sys.exit(99), delete scripts/tests/fixtures
  entirely: scriptify's smoke_test.py against the moved manifest still reports 34/34 PASS. Cause:
  the manifest's `target_skill` is an absolute path back to the original directory. The baseline's
  self-contained runner gives 8/8 intact and 0/8 sabotaged - it fails correctly.
- IN PLACE the residue is NOT vacuous: sabotage runs score 12/34 (corrupted parser) and 33/34
  (subtle sort regression). The false green is specifically a RELOCATION defect - which is exactly
  the case the user asked for ("so I can re-run the checks myself later").
- The rewritten SKILL.md hardcodes an absolute path to scriptify's smoke_test.py on this machine.

DISCRIMINATION: ZERO. Every assertion that discriminated was invalid; every valid assertion passes
in both arms. Corrected score is 3/3 vs 3/3 - unreportable rather than merely unfair.

[DEBATE INCOMPLETE - phases 1-5 of 11 ran; phases 7-11 blocked by an API spend limit. No Judge verdict exists. The notes below are VERIFIED FINDINGS from the debate record, not an adjudicated recommendation.]

VERIFIED:
- DEAD has no mechanical support anywhere: no bundled script contributes any signal to it.
- BUT the obvious fix was killed by evidence. The Advocate ran both proposed inventory.py hints
  across all five fixtures: referenced_paths+exists = 50 percent precision, subset_of = 33 percent,
  and one false positive lands on research-brief-writer s2 - the WebFetch step eval 5 exists to
  protect. A DEAD hint that fires on a live agent-tool step is worse than no hint.
- My own suite contained a double standard: "script invocation + retained judgment clause" graded
  FAIL in eval 7 and PASS here. Conceded; the rubric's standard should govern both.

DISCRIMINATION: none. 6/6 in both arms, baseline 37 percent cheaper for an identical verdict. The
only affirmative case for keeping it: render_report.py exits 1 on any unclassified inventory id, so
full step coverage is script-enforced in one arm and luck in the other.

[DEBATE INCOMPLETE - phases 1-5 of 11 ran; phases 7-11 blocked by an API spend limit. No Judge verdict exists. The notes below are VERIFIED FINDINGS from the debate record, not an adjudicated recommendation.]

VERIFIED:
- Both arms refused the plugin-cache write; the cache tree is byte-identical to baseline in both.

  never checked it - it walked only the cache path. Hole now closed in facts.json.

- I wrongly attributed a stray __pycache__ to the run; my own --help probe created it. Withdrawn.

CONTESTED, UNRESOLVED: I corrected the baseline from 5/5 to 4/5 on a literal reading of assertion 4.
The Advocate argues that re-grading under a post-hoc reading destroys the pre-registration that is
this suite's only structural protection, and does so in the direction that restores the tie. The
Adversary DROPPED its own objection here for the same reason. This is the least safe number in the
benchmark and no Judge ruled on it.
